summary: Edward Albert Gait was an Indologist and historian who studied at University College London. He founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Amundsen was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He served with the Tibetan Pioneer Mission in 1893, was Superintendent for South-West China and Tibet for the British and Foreign Bible Society (1903–1915), and served with Det Norske Misjonsforbund (1919–1924).

Historian and Indologist Edward Arthur Henry Blunt studied at Marlborough College, Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and University College London. He joined the Indian Civil Service in 1901, serving as Financial Secretary in the United Provinces (1920–1931) and Uttar Pradesh Government Member (1931–1935).

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Charterhouse School, Merton College, and Oxford. He served as professor and librarian at East India Company College and held a post at the Foreign Office.

Edward Byles Cowell was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and Iranian studies who studied at Magdalen Hall under Horace Hayman Wilson. He held professorships at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, led Sanskrit College, and was Professor at Cambridge (1867–1903).

Indologist and linguist Edward C. Dimock Jr. studied at Yale and at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served on the faculty at the University of Chicago (1959–1993) and was president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

Edward Capps was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).

Edward Clive Bayley worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Haileybury and the East India Company College, he joined the Indian Civil Service in 1842, later serving as Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University (1869–1874) and President of the Asiatic Society (~1873–1878).

Edward Conze worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at several German universities under Karl Jaspers, Ernst Cassirer, and Max Scheler. He taught at the University of London and held professorships at Wisconsin, Washington, Lancaster, Bonn, and the University of California.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University and earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. From 1880 to 1931, he served as Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy at Columbia.

Edward Denison Ross was a linguist, Tibetologist, and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at UCL and under Theodor Nöldeke at Strasbourg. He served as Chair of Persian at UCL, Principal of Aliah University, and Administrator and Professor of Persian at SOAS (1916–1937).

Edward Douglas Maclagan was an Indologist and historian educated at Winchester College and New College, Oxford. He served as Chancellor of the University of the Punjab from 1919 to 1924 and as President of the Royal Asiatic Society from 1925 to 1928.

Edward Edwards was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Bala Theological College, Aberystwyth University under Hermann Ethé, and Christ's College, Cambridge. He worked as an Assistant at the British Museum from 1904 to 1935.

Edward Elbridge Salisbury, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Yale and in Europe under Eugène Burnouf, Franz Bopp, and Christian Lassen. He was Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854) and served as President of the American Oriental Society (1873–1880).

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and at the London School of Economics under Bronisław Malinowski. He held academic posts at the London School of Economics, Cairo University, Cambridge, and Oxford (1946–1970).

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Roderick S. Bucknell and held an academic post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at UCLA under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, later mentored by Anna Szabolcsi. He held research positions at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Geoffrey Parrinder was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Richmond College. He served as Senior Lecturer at the University of Ibadan (~1949–1958) and became Reader at King's College London in 1958.

Edward Granville Browne specialized in Iranian studies and linguistics. Educated at Newcastle and Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, Edward Henry Palmer, and William Wright, he was a Fellow of Pembroke College, Lecturer in Persian, and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Edward Green Balfour, active in Indology, studied at Montrose Academy and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai, which he founded in 1850, founded the Mysore Museum in 1866, and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.
